wiz.title: New certificate
wiz.connect.title: First, connect Advanced ACME to DSM
wiz.connect.intro: To install certificates in DSM, Advanced ACME needs a DSM account. This is set up only once; afterwards you choose your certificate provider.
wiz.provider.title: Where should the certificate come from?
wiz.provider.intro: If your domain is at IONOS and your contract includes SSL certificates, choose IONOS SSL.
wiz.account.title: Connect to {provider}
wiz.account.ionos_step1: Log in to {link} and open SSL certificates.
wiz.account.ionos_step2: Click “ACME External Account Bindings” in the menu on the right and create a new account. Enter any name, for example “NAS”.
wiz.account.ionos_step3: IONOS now shows a Key ID and an HMAC key. Copy both into the fields below.
wiz.account.ionos_step4: Important: the HMAC key is shown only once. Paste it here right away.
wiz.account.ionos_step5: Already using this certificate, set up by hand? Then link it to ACME first: open {link}, choose “Manage” for the certificate, then “Advanced settings” > “Migrate to ACME”, and select the External Account Binding you just created.
wiz.account.ionos_note: Your IONOS account needs a free DV certificate slot, and the domain must use the IONOS name servers.
wiz.account.le_intro: Let's Encrypt does not need an account. Click “Connect” to create one automatically.
wiz.account.zerossl_intro: ZeroSSL links the certificates to your e-mail address.
wiz.account.custom_intro: Enter the ACME directory URL of your certificate provider. Some providers also require External Account Binding data (Key ID and HMAC key).
wiz.account.server_help: Usually ends with /directory. Your provider lists it in its ACME documentation.
wiz.account.hmac_help: Used to link the NAS to your account. It is stored protected on the NAS together with the other access data.
wiz.account.eab_optional: Only if your provider requires External Account Binding.

wiz.account.already_connected: The NAS is already connected to this provider.
wiz.dns.title: How should the domain be confirmed?
wiz.dns.intro: The provider checks that the domain belongs to you. Advanced ACME creates a short-lived DNS entry for this automatically. Your NAS does not need to be reachable from the internet.

wiz.dns.ionos_step2: Create a new API key. IONOS shows a public prefix and a secret.
wiz.dns.ionos_step3: Copy both values into the fields below and click “Check”.

wiz.dsm.title: Installation in DSM
wiz.summary.title: Everything ready
wiz.summary.note: Requesting the certificate usually takes one to three minutes. After that, Advanced ACME renews it automatically before it expires and installs it in DSM.
wiz.summary.success: The certificate was created and installed in DSM.
wiz.summary.success_next: Tip: in DSM under Control Panel > Security > Certificate > Settings you choose which services use the certificate, for example the DSM desktop.
dsm.intro: To install certificates, Advanced ACME signs in to DSM like you do. Please enter a DSM administrator account. The data is stored protected on the NAS and is only used to install certificates.
dsm.dedicated_1: In DSM, open Control Panel > User & Group and create a user, for example “certbot”, with a long random password.
dsm.dedicated_2: Add the user to the “administrators” group.
dsm.dedicated_3: In the next steps, deny access to all shared folders and applications for this user.
dsm.dedicated_4: Enter this user here. You can then change your own password at any time without affecting renewals.

dsm.renewable_warning: DSM renews this certificate itself (Let's Encrypt). Better choose another one, otherwise DSM may overwrite it.
dsm.mode_auto_help: Advanced ACME creates its own DSM account with a random password. Your password is not stored.
dsm.mode_existing_help: For experts: enter a DSM administrator account that you have set up yourself.

expert.title: Expert mode: acme.sh
expert.intro: Here you work directly with the original acme.sh. The package keeps its data in its own folder and uses no system files, so DSM updates are not affected. Certificates created here appear in the overview, and the service renews them automatically.

expert.examples: Examples (to install in DSM use the deploy hook advanced_acme_dsm):

expert.hook_info: The deploy hook advanced_acme_dsm uses the DSM account from Settings and the original synology_dsm hook of acme.sh. It is saved per certificate, so renewals install automatically.
help.title: Help
help.how.a: Advanced ACME requests certificates with the proven open-source client acme.sh using the ACME protocol. The domain is confirmed through a short-lived DNS entry, so the NAS does not need to be reachable from the internet. The finished certificate is installed through the official DSM interface and appears in Control Panel > Security > Certificate like any other certificate. A package service checks twice a day whether a renewal is due.
help.ionos180.a: Since 10 March 2026, IONOS issues SSL certificates with a technical validity of 180 days instead of one year. Your contract and billing are not affected. Manually installed certificates would have to be replaced twice a year. With Advanced ACME this happens automatically through the IONOS ACME server.
help.updates.q: Is this safe for DSM updates?
help.updates.a: Yes. Advanced ACME is a normal DSM package. It runs as its own user without root rights, uses no cron jobs and changes no system files. All data is kept in the package's own folder, which survives DSM and package updates.
help.dsm_gui.q: Why is this not built into the DSM certificate dialog?
help.dsm_gui.a: The DSM certificate dialog is part of the operating system. Changing it would be overwritten by every DSM update and could make updates fail. Advanced ACME therefore uses the official DSM interface: the certificates end up in the normal DSM certificate management, where you assign them to services as usual.
help.security.q: Where are my access data stored?
help.security.a: The DNS API key, the DSM account and the External Account Binding data (Key ID and HMAC key) are stored in the package's data folder, which only the package user can read. Only DSM administrators can open Advanced ACME.
help.dsm_account.q: Why does Advanced ACME create a DSM account?
help.dsm_account.a: DSM lets only administrators install certificates, so Advanced ACME has to sign in as an administrator. So that your own password is never stored, the assistant creates the separate account “advanced-acme” with a long random password. It is listed in Control Panel > User & Group. Remove it with “Remove account” in Settings; if you uninstall the package and delete its data, it is deleted as well.
help.dsm_task.a: If DSM requires 2-step verification for all administrators, Advanced ACME cannot use an account of its own. Instead it can create the task “Advanced ACME” in the DSM Task Scheduler. It runs every minute as root and installs renewed certificates with DSM's own tools, as DSM does for Let's Encrypt. Its script is stored in the task, runs no files of the package and only reads the certificates handed over. When you remove it in Advanced ACME or uninstall the package, it deletes itself. Every step is listed under Settings > History.
help.default.q: How do I use the certificate for the DSM desktop?
help.default.a: Either choose to replace the current default certificate in the assistant, or open Control Panel > Security > Certificate in DSM, select the certificate and set it as default, or assign it to individual services under Settings. Assignments stay in place after every renewal.
help.uninstall.q: What happens if I uninstall the package?
help.uninstall.a: The certificates installed in DSM remain, but they are no longer renewed. In the uninstall dialog you choose whether the stored access data and acme.sh data are deleted (preselected). If you keep them, a later reinstallation continues with them.
help.dns01.a: IONOS is set up with a guided form. In addition, all DNS providers supported by acme.sh can be selected, more than 200, for example Cloudflare, Hetzner, INWX, netcup or deSEC.

acme.title: acme.sh version
acme.intro: Advanced ACME is tested with the bundled acme.sh {bundled}. You can install newer official acme.sh releases. The bundled version always stays available, and you can return to it at any time.
acme.experimental: Experimental: acme.sh {version} is active. Advanced ACME has only been tested with the bundled acme.sh {bundled}. Newer versions usually work, but changes in acme.sh can affect issuing or installing certificates. If something stops working, return to the bundled version.
